pins.title: Kenton's dive shop
pins.description: Kenton's beach shop on Key Lento, Mariana County. Finish the Chapter 1 story mission "Island Dreams" here to unlock treasure diving, one of the best early money makers.

pins.title: Treasure dive sites
pins.description: After Island Dreams, purple chest icons mark shipwreck dive sites around the Keys. Take Kenton's boat out and dive with scuba gear and a metal detector.

pins.title: Moses: car buyer
pins.description: Moses buys stolen cars in Port Gellhorn, Kelly County. Unlocks in Chapter 2. Cars with a tracker won't sell here, so pick older models.

pins.title: Tyrone: fence
pins.description: Fence in La Perle, Vice City, from Chapter 3. Pays the most for narcotics.

pins.title: Yasmani: fence
pins.description: Fence in Little Cuba, Vice City, from Chapter 3. Pays the most for jewelry and marked bills.

pins.title: Hamlet gun store
pins.description: Gun store in Hamlet, Vice-Dale County, on the city's edge. Weapons, ammo and body armor.

pins.title: Pawn & Gun, Port Gellhorn
pins.description: Pawn and gun store in Port Gellhorn, Kelly County. Handy before missions up the coast.

pins.title: Rideout Customs
pins.description: Vice City mod shop for custom rims, interiors and show-car builds. Ultimate Edition owners only.

pins.title: One-Eyed Willie's
pins.description: Off-road mod shop at Lake Leonida with hand-painted finishes. Ultimate Edition owners only.

pins.title: Treasure diving playbook
pins.description: Seven shipwreck sets around the Keys, each worth tens of thousands. Five count toward 100%, and all seven complete Underwater Discoveries. Dive in daylight, sweep the detector slowly, surface before oxygen runs out, and sell to Kenton after every set.

pins.title: Randy: high-end cars
pins.description: Randy in Balsero, Vice City, buys high-end cars that carry advanced trackers. Unlocks in Chapter 3 after the mission where you steal the Zorrusso for him. Your best payout for stolen cars.

pins.title: Fence cheat sheet
pins.description: Don't sell everything to one buyer. Narcotics go to Tyrone in La Perle; jewelry and marked bills go to Yasmani in Little Cuba. Early fences in the Keys pay very little, so hold your loot until Chapter 3 if you can.

pins.title: Garage drop-off trick
pins.description: From Chapter 3, once Yasmani is unlocked, drop stolen goods at your nearest garage and pick which fence buys them. Your partner drives off and sells them for you. No more long drives across the map.

pins.title: Pay 'n' Spray, Hamlet
pins.description: Hot car? Drive in for a respray and the cops lose track of you. Pay 'n' Spray also repairs cars and registers ones you want to keep. 19 shops across Leonida, 5 around Vice City.

pins.title: Key Lento bank
pins.description: A small bank in the Keys, close to Jason's home. Low payout (about $5K–$20K) but a good first bank job. Bank cash comes out as marked bills, so sell it to a fence.

pins.title: Persistence Road Garage
pins.description: Garage in western Bellville, north of Vice City. Buy it through the Vice City Real Estate app once Chapter 2 unlocks it.

pins.title: How to lose the cops
pins.description: Break line of sight first: get out of the search cones on your minimap. Then head to a Pay 'n' Spray and respray, or swap cars.

pins.title: Bank job money route
pins.description: Leonida has 22 bank jobs: 14 small banks and 8 big vaults. Start small in the Keys, then work up to the big vaults in Ocean Beach and Downtown Vice City, which pay six figures. All bank cash is marked bills, and Yasmani in Little Cuba pays the most for them.

pins.title: Garage buying order
pins.description: Garages are the only property you can buy. From Chapter 2, open the Vice City Real Estate app. There are 8 for sale, from $4K to $40K (about $160K for all). Buy cheap ones first for storage, then a Vice City garage close to the action.

pins.title: Bank cash, fast
pins.description: Don't drive marked bills around. Once Yasmani is unlocked in Chapter 3, drop the loot at your nearest garage and send it to him. Your partner sells it while you start the next job.

pins.title: Jason's cash stash
pins.description: Before you unlock the BuckMe bank app, hide cash under the loose floorboards in Jason's bedroom at his Key Lento stilt house. Walk into the bedroom and look for the prompt to inspect the floorboards.

pins.title: Don't die holding cash
pins.description: Cash in your pocket is gone if you die or get busted. Deposit it in BuckMe (unlocks in Chapter 1) or at an ATM before any risky job. Heads up: Family Savings can't be withdrawn.

pins.title: Dye Pack Jammer first
pins.description: Don't rob a bank or payday loan store yet. Fences refuse marked bills until you get the Dye Pack Jammer from the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check (Meet Raul's Crew).

pins.title: Vault payday
pins.description: Big bank vaults pay up to about $205,000 in marked bills, but you get 4 wanted stars the moment you start. Have your escape car ready, then sell the bills to Yasmani in Little Cuba.

pins.title: Gang hideouts
pins.description: Yellow hideout icons on your map are gang stash houses (Illegal Operations). Each holds cash, jewelry or drugs, worth about $1,000 to $2,000 early on. Sell drugs and jewelry to a fence.

pins.title: Crack any store safe
pins.description: Safe codes are random every time, so online code lists won't work. Look for a sticky note, papers or a computer screen in the back office, check downed guards, or make staff tell you.

pins.title: Red stars aren't safe
pins.description: Red stars mean you escaped the chase but you're still inside the police search area. Leave the red zone on your map, change clothes or swap cars, and don't come back to that block until it fades.

pins.title: Sell early, Keys fences close
pins.description: Brian and Donnie, the first fences in the Keys, are early-story only and pay very low. Don't stockpile loot for them; Dunk, Tyrone and Yasmani stay open for good.

pins.title: Hideout drugs to Tyrone
pins.description: Drugs you take from gang hideouts sell best to Tyrone in La Perle (unlocks in Chapter 3), who pays the top rate for narcotics. Early fences pay low for the same bag.

pins.title: Jewelry to Yasmani
pins.description: Jewelry store robberies open through Yasmani's jobs in Chapter 3, and Yasmani in Little Cuba pays the top rate for jewelry. Don't sell to the nearest fence.

pins.title: Moses only takes clean cars
pins.description: Moses in Port Gellhorn buys stolen cars only if they have no tracker. Scan the car with the WAINK app on your phone before you drive it over.

pins.title: Follow the cash truck in
pins.description: Bank vaults only open when a cash truck arrives, so wait for the delivery and enter the vault while it's open. Get the Dye Pack Jammer first (see the Dye Pack pin).

pins.title: Chapter 1 cash gets wiped
pins.description: Whatever cash you build up in Chapter 1 is gone when the chapter ends. Don't grind for money early. Push the story and save your big money runs for Chapter 2 and later.

pins.title: Plane crash loot
pins.description: See a plane trailing smoke over Grassrivers? Chase it to the wreck. Most crash sites have about $1,000 in product on the ground, plus a flare gun on a nearby body. Rival crews and cops show up within minutes, so grab it and go.

pins.title: Exotic Animals Front stash
pins.description: Do your neighbor Shirley's errand: buy her rum at the Key Lento liquor store. Come back, climb the fence beside the store into the courtyard and clear the yard. The parrot tips you off: about $1,300 is in the vent by the generator. The backroom safe holds about $900 and the register $100, roughly $2,300 total.

pins.title: Vice-Dale warehouse jackpot
pins.description: A free-roam warehouse about three miles south of Hamlet, worth roughly $13,000 in cash and product. The office safe holds a rare Leroy Rook card that a pawn shop buys for about $6,000. It's heavily guarded and the cops come fast, so park a quick getaway car outside. Weapons inside: Type 9 SMG by the entrance, Duke 556 rifle near a body, Kalinga 50 pistol in the office.

pins.title: Tiger motel safe
pins.description: Rundown motel south of Hamlet. Follow the screaming. There's a loose tiger inside. Get past it and the safe holds over $1,000, with about $640 in product on a nearby table. The weapon case has the Laird 350 sniper rifle.

pins.title: Stalled-car stash bags
pins.description: Stop for drivers with broken-down cars anywhere in Leonida. If they tell you to get lost, the car is a front. Check the trunk for a duffel with about $1,280 in product. It's repeatable. Sell at Brian's Lockup, which pays into your mailbox the next day.

guides.title: How to use Millionaire's Row
guides.summary: Map, checklists and guides — and how they update.
body: The map shows every discovered location by category. Tap the filters at the top to show only what you’re hunting for, then tap a pin for details.
Checklists save your progress on this device. Tick items off as you go and watch your completion percentage climb.
Content updates live. As players discover new locations after Nov 19, they appear here without needing an app update.

guides.title: Money-making basics for open-world crime games
guides.summary: The principles that carry over to every game in the genre.
body: Big open-world crime games almost always reward the same habits. Until we confirm the specifics in-game, these are the safest bets:
• Finish story missions early — they usually unlock the best income sources.
• Invest in businesses or properties when they appear; passive income adds up.
• Don’t overspend on cars and outfits in the first hours.
• Save before risky jobs so a failed attempt doesn’t cost you.
We’ll replace this with tested, game-specific methods as soon as the game is out.
